sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Jay Singh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
The FIR in question was lodged by the informant alleging that the daughter of the informant was killed by the applicant.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased and is in custody since 30.10.2019.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.

3. The Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the statement of the informant who has declared hostile and the PW 2, who is the brother of the deceased has also turned hostile.
4.
Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

Yogendra vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171832270/
1

5. Considering In view of the said two statements of the informant and the PW 2 coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody for almost 4 years and the applicant has no criminal antecedents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
7. Let the applicant Yogendra be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.219 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of the DP Act, Police Station Barkhera, District Philibhit on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
